caption_used: Training rewards of LLaMA-3.1 8B on the Easy and Hard training sets, displayed as two vertically stacked line plots. In the Easy Training Set (top panel), both Llama-On-Policy-Easy (teal) and Llama-LUFFY-Easy (red) start near 0.0 and increase over 500 steps, with LUFFY reaching approximately 0.4 and On-Policy reaching approximately 0.35 at step 500. In the Hard Training Set (bottom panel), Llama-LUFFY-Hard shows steady improvement from near 0.0 to approximately 0.2 by step 500, while Llama-On-Policy-Hard initially rises to approximately 0.05 before declining back toward 0.0 after step 150. Notably, the performance gap between the two methods is substantially wider on the Easy set, where LUFFY maintains a consistent lead of approximately 0.10 throughout training, compared to the Hard set where their trajectories only clearly diverge after step 200.

The figure presents two vertically stacked line plots comparing the training rewards of two algorithms, Llama-On-Policy and Llama-LUFFY, across Easy and Hard training sets. Both plots share the same x-axis labeled "Steps," ranging from 0 to 500 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 100. The y-axis is labeled "Training Rewards" and uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 0.4 in the top plot and 0.0 to 0.2 in the bottom plot. In the top plot, titled "Easy Training Set," the teal line represents Llama-On-Policy-Easy, starting near 0.0 and increasing to approximately 0.35 at step 500. The red line represents Llama-LUFFY-Easy, starting near 0.0 and increasing to approximately 0.4 at step 500. Both lines exhibit upward trends with some fluctuation, and the red line remains consistently above the teal line. In the bottom plot, titled "Hard Training Set," the teal line for Llama-On-Policy-Hard starts near 0.0, rises to approximately 0.05 by step 100, and then declines back toward 0.0 after step 150, remaining near zero thereafter. The red line for Llama-LUFFY-Hard starts near 0.0, increases steadily to approximately 0.2 by step 500, and shows some minor fluctuations. Both lines are solid with no markers, and the red line remains consistently above the teal line throughout the entire range. The shaded regions around each line represent the uncertainty or standard deviation of the rewards. The performance gap between the two methods is visibly wider in the Easy set compared to the Hard set, where their trajectories diverge more clearly after step 200.
